final_trade_decision:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is a staged accumulate, not a chase. Take a 25% starter near 180.38, hold the bulk of the allocation (40%) for the 177.10–178.35 VWMA/10-EMA confluence with partials into 176.82 and the 173.30–173.52 shelf, and release the final 35% only on a daily close above 181.70 with volume ≥45M shares and the MACD histogram flipping positive. Use a close-based stop under 171.47 (never inside the 179.3–180.2 noise band given ATR 3.26), with a close below 165.74 as thesis-level invalidation, and size the aggregate so a slide from average cost to 171.47 costs no more than ~1.5% of portfolio value. Scale partials into 186–188, full measured-move target ~197.7.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is decided by the fundamental inflection, which the bear conceded outright ("the 10-K is real… I accept the data"): four consecutive quarters of accelerating revenue (9.4% → 10.8% → 12.6% → 13.9%) on a ~$575B base, operating income roughly tripled ($12.2B → $36.9B), a record 6.4% operating margin above the 2020 peak, record 47.0% gross margin, and FCF swinging ~+$49B to +$32.2B with FCF/net income at 1.06x — cash-backed earnings power, not an accrual story. The balance sheet repaired alongside it (current ratio 0.94x → 1.05x, cash +36% to $73.4B, liabilities/equity 2.17x → 1.61x). The primary trend confirms it: 180.38 > 10 EMA 178.35 > 50 SMA 170.51 > 200 SMA 145.58, all rising, with ascending March lows 171.47 → 179.26 and price above a rising VWMA of 177.10.

Why Overweight and not Buy: the bear's objection is entry-timing, and on that specific point the evidence supports it. AMZN sits at a new 2024 closing high, +23.9% above the 200 SMA, with ~1.3% to the 181.70 ceiling versus 3–5% to meaningful support; the 3/28 high pierced the upper Bollinger band (181.70 vs 181.513) and closed back inside; March volume ~36M versus 45–50M+ in February; MACD still in a bearish cross (2.547 vs 2.599, histogram –0.053); RSI 61.90 against February peaks of 73.78/72.43 is a mild negative divergence; ATR 3.26 (1.8% of price) means one ordinary session can cut both the 10 EMA and the VWMA. The bear also correctly flags sequencing risk the bull downplays: ~87% of FY2023 FCF landed in Q4, so Q1–Q3'24 FCF prints will look poor against the FY run-rate, the capex cut (–17.2% to $52.7B) is the exhaustible half of the FCF story, 400bps of margin expansion is not repeatable, and H2'24 laps 7.8% operating-margin comps. None of this breaks the thesis; together they argue against paying up inside the 179.26–181.70 band, which is exactly why the rating is Overweight with tranche discipline rather than a full-size Buy.

The Trader's proposal is consistent with the research plan and internally coherent: starter at the last close, bulk of capital at the VWMA/10-EMA confluence, breakout tranche gated on both volume and MACD confirmation, and a structural stop placed ~2.7 ATR below entry rather than inside the noise band. No risk-management debate was conducted, so I assessed the proposal directly — the stop level (171.47) and the ~1.5% portfolio risk budget are appropriate for ATR of 3.26, and imply a full-size notional of roughly 30% of portfolio value (1.5% ÷ ~4.9% stop distance); a caller who finds that too large should shrink the position rather than widen the stop.

Explicit information gaps I am not papering over: no valuation multiples (market cap, P/E, EV/EBITDA withheld), no insider-transaction data, no AWS/advertising segment breakdown, and an incomplete sentiment read (1 of 3 sources, Neutral 5.1). The missing multiple is symmetric — neither side can prove AMZN cheap or expensive — so it caps conviction at Overweight rather than Buy.

What would change the call: (a) a failed breakout — rejection of 181.70 on volume ≥45M with a close back below 177.10; (b) 10Y decisively above 4.34%, which caps the multiple regardless of fundamentals; (c) a weak Q1'24 FCF print accompanied by commentary implying the Q4 concentration was not seasonal (a merely weak FCF headline alone is expected seasonality and not a sell); (d) valuation data emerging that shows AMZN at a clear premium to its own history without matching earnings revisions; (e) a close below 165.74, the post-gap February low, which breaks the structural uptrend and triggers a full exit.

**Price Target**: 197.7

**Time Horizon**: 6-12 months
